note: Two family campgrounds on an island where the Fisher River meets the Chippewa: the South Campground has the electric sites and the shower building; the North Campground has no electric, with many sites along the river or its quiet lagoons under the trees. The park links to the Old Abe State Trail. --Claude
summary: DNR park, camping and conditions pages and the campground map read; GoingToCamp unread (refuses). 69 sites (South 1E-24E all electric; North 25-69 none), showers/flush toilets in the South loop, vault toilets and water in the North. Riverfront not earned: every shore is under continuous canopy and no site can be placed on open ground -> riverview lead. Pin ~700 m north of the South (electric) campground it claims to mark.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (riverfront -> riverview): the DNR says 'many of the 45 campsites [North Campground] are on the shoreline of the Chippewa River or its bays', but on Esri and USGS imagery the whole island is under continuous hardwood-conifer canopy down to the water; no campsite, pad or loop is visible and none can be placed on open ground within ~50 m (GoingToCamp, which holds the site photos and map coordinates, refuses). The North loop seems to run between the river's backwater bays (the 'bays' are lagoons). Under the canopy rule and 'unsure -> down', the shoreline sites are a river view. The South (electric) campground is inland.

PIN: stored 45.1820,-91.1685 is in unbroken forest ~700 m NNE of OpenStreetMap's 'Brunet Island State Park Campground' node (45.17604,-91.17168, on the 'Brunet Camping Area' loop roads at the island's south end), which is the South (electric) campground the note says the pin marks. Suggest 45.1760,-91.1717. The North Campground lies further north (the DNR map puts it ~350 m north of the South loop); its loop is not visible under canopy.
